messages:
incident-bot: ALERT sev2: sudden rise in `token_mismatch` and `cross_request_kv_hits` for model rdx-7b-qlora-prod across long-payload endpoints (/v1/generate, /v1/stream). Suspected kv-cache reuse correctness regression.

incident-bot: affected_regions=[us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1], spike_start=2055552400, current_rate=0.08 (8% of long-streams).

Lina Zhao: paging on-call Tomás. this looks like the continuous-batching + kv reuse path we toggled in 2.14. can you pick this up?

Tomás Rivera: oncall here. seeing tail of `wrong_seq_offset` traces in honeycomb and a cluster of garbled completions. prioritizing investigation.

Priya Nair: support: several customers reporting interleaved tokens in separate requests. example from HealthSync (redacted): "...patient id 42..." mixed into unrelated prompt. clear token bleed. Marking P0 for privacy review.

Evan Brooks: wtf. Is this the same pattern as the paging regression we fixed in canary a while back?

Tomás Rivera: similar surface but not identical. earlier issue was cache eviction; this looks like stale per-shard last_offset being reused across different request session ids when continuous-batching splits pages.

Sienna Park: I'm with security — if customer-specific tokens leak across sessions we need to escalate to legal + compliance. Priya, can you DM the transcript?

Priya Nair: sent to secure channel. initial manual redaction applied.

Tomás Rivera: quick triage: 1) reproduce locally with long-stream workload and mixed small/large concurrent requests to same model instance 2) confirm whether kv shard metadata stores request_id or only offset 3) check code path introduced in runtime v2.14 that flips on KV_CACHE_REUSE.

Lina Zhao: mitigation options: A) immediate feature-flag disable kv_cache_reuse, B) apply runtime patch to validate request boundary before reuse (risky to hotfix without tests), C) divert traffic to non-reuse pool. Thoughts?

Evan Brooks: A is safest and fastest. flips and a rolling restart. we can do a controlled regional roll. C requires capacity and provisioning.

Tomás Rivera: I'll run a canary disable in us-west-2 and monitor `cross_request_kv_hits`.

Tomás Rivera: command:```sh
# disable reuse in region
redwoodctl feature disable kv_cache_reuse --env=prod --region=us-west-2 --reason="incident-2055552468"
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag "kv_cache_reuse" disabled in prod/us-west-2 by Tomás Rivera (run id: dpl-9972).

Tomás Rivera: draining inference nodes in us-west-2. kubectl drain commands issued for pool-rdx-7b-1. waiting for graceful handoff of active sessions.

Priya Nair: support note: messaging to customers: "We identified an issue affecting long-stream requests where token sequences could be mixed across concurrent sessions. We have applied an interim mitigation and recommend retrying in 10 minutes. A postmortem will follow." Sending now.

Sienna Park: security: please capture full set of affected transcripts in secure S3 with ACLs and notify compliance. If any PHI observed, we escalate immediately.

Evan Brooks: metrics update: 3m after disable in us-west-2 `token_mismatch` down 70%. us-east-1 still high.

Tomás Rivera: proceeding to disable in us-east-1.```sh
redwoodctl feature disable kv_cache_reuse --env=prod --region=us-east-1 --reason="incident-2055552468"
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag "kv_cache_reuse" disabled in prod/us-east-1 by Tomás Rivera (run id: dpl-9973).

Lina Zhao: coordinate with infra: please pause autoscaler and any burst scale-ups to avoid regeneration storms while we restart pools.

Evan Brooks: doing:```sh
redwoodctl autoscaler hold --env=prod --duration=15m --reason="incident-2055552468"
```

Tomás Rivera: restarts in us-west-2 and us-east-1 underway. eu-west-1 scheduled last.

Priya Nair: HealthSync confirms improvement but reported one lingering bad completion at 2055552508. I uploaded that transcript to s3://rdw-incident/2055552468/HealthSync-1.txt (access: security+support).

Sienna Park: received. initial check: token bleed confined to tokens generated during streaming windows; no evidence of database-level exposure. escalating to legal as precaution.

Tomás Rivera: root-cause hypothesis: shard_cache stores {last_offset, kv_ptr} but not a session tag. continuous-batching fragmenter can emit pages that mix sequences when small fast requests race with long streaming ones. fix: attach session_id + monotonic offset check to cached entry and reject reuse when mismatch.

Evan Brooks: that sounds right. timeline for a proper patch?

Tomás Rivera: I can open a PR with tests by EOD. but we need an integration scenario: mixed small/large concurrent traffic and paging boundaries. Ben from runtime perf can help add test harness.

Lina Zhao: assign owners: Tomás + Evan for patch, Sienna + Priya for security/customer comms, Lina to lead postmortem and timeline, deploy-bot to orchestrate canary when patch ready.

Tomás Rivera: started branch: fixes/kv-session-boundary-205555. basic change: store request_guid on shard cache entries and validate on reuse. adding metric `cache_reuse_ownership_failures` to detect real-time attempts.

Tomás Rivera: code snippet (pseudo):```python
entry = shard_cache.get(key)
if entry and entry.session_guid == req.session_guid and entry.offset <= req.start:
    use(entry.kv)
else:
    record_metric("cache_reuse_ownership_failures")
    load_kv_from_store()
```

Evan Brooks: good. also add e2e test that simulates continuous-batching splitting and asserts no cross-session tokens ever returned.

Priya Nair: support update sent: customers asked to re-run failing requests. most report improvement after region restarts. I'll keep collecting edge transcripts.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for branch fixes/kv-session-boundary-205555 (5% traffic, long-stream workload).

Tomás Rivera: canary started 2055552580. monitoring dashboards: `token_mismatch` at 0.01 in canary, `cache_reuse_ownership_failures` = 23 (expected during rollout as metric trips).

Sienna Park: security review note: low-probability PII exposure limited to token-level mixing; legal notified and will await postmortem.

Lina Zhao: timeline for postmortem: collect start time 2055552400, detection 2055552468, mitigation (flag disable/regional restarts) 2055552475-2055552550, canary patch deployed 2055552580. I'll spin up a 60-min war room doc and tag for next steps.

Evan Brooks: after patch validated, plan to re-enable kv_cache_reuse with strict ownership checks and a throttle: gradual ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, with `cache_reuse_ownership_failures` alarm cutover.

Tomás Rivera: marking incident as mitigated while feature flag remains off in prod global. will update last_message_ts when full roll forward completes.

Priya Nair: closing loop with customers: HealthSync and FinLogix are satisfied with interim mitigation. I'll prepare a joint remediation note.

Lina Zhao: thanks team. good triage. we'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and action items (tests, metrics, docs). If any new reports come in, ping here.
